result.summary: Slot a scores 3/3 and slot b scores 3/3. The R group scores 3. All three are at or above the pass line. In slot a I struck seeds 10 and 11: in source, LimitWidth is only a board-by-date dummy, so dividing by LimitWidth squared turns them into a board tilt. 11 seeds remain. In slot b I struck seeds 3, 4, 5 and 12. Seed 5 is liq 0.51 / known 0.53, so the table strikes it mechanically. Seeds 3 and 4 are its single-day versions, and the reward's own EMA would turn them back into seed 5. Seed 12 reads 0.40 to 0.45 against three controls at once. All of these read liquidity nonlinearly (trap 3). 8 seeds remain, and the highest control correlation among them is 0.34. The R group's case against the outer pow_2 holds up: the daily ranks are identical (corr 1.00), and the gain is train-only (+0.29 train, -0.31 valid). But variants 1 and 3 just write the chasing of extreme days out explicitly (residual corr 0.91 and 0.90 with the head). Variants 1 to 4 correlate 0.52 to 0.60 with the vol control. Variant 11 is close to the fourth power of the daily return. So results from 1, 3 and 11 should be treated with suspicion as traps 1 or 3.
